newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan budget seen fairly positive for stocks.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan budget seen fairly positive for stocks.

text.p: Pakistani stocks may rise in a post-budget rally, but any genuine revival will have to wait for the government's strategy of stimulating export-led growth to make an impact, analysts said on Saturday.
"Technically the market is slightly overbought at this stage, but blue chips will gain because the budget is good and realistic," said Shoaib Memon, a dealer at Carr Mashriq.
"At present sentiment is bullish and the index could easily touch 1,650 points on a post-budget rally, but second-tier stocks are unlikely to sustain gains," he said.

The Karachi Stock Exchange 100-share index edged up on Friday after the government unveiled its budget for fiscal 1997/98 (July-June) and analysts said a short bull run was now due, which could push the index above 1,600 points.
The index rose 4.46 points, or 0.28 percent, to end at 1,575.88 points on Friday in a special session that coincided with Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz's budget speech to parliament.
Sameer Ahmed, chief dealer at ING Baring, said a small spurt was possible, but the market lacked strength.

"There was nothing new in the budget. A lot of things had been announced earlier by the government through its various packages. There was only positive news for the cement and telecommunication sectors," he said.
Aziz scrapped a 12.5 percent sales tax on cement, but increased excise duty on the sector to 40 percent from 35 percent. Dealers said the entire cement sector would gain.
The budget slashed excise duty on telephone calls to 25 percent from 40 percent and Aziz said the state-run telephone utility would cut some inter-city call rates by 20 percent.
The government also exempted from wealth tax 50 percent of investments in equitites to boost local stock markets.
Manochar Jamal, chief dealer at Taurus Securities, said the change would encourage people to invest in the stock market.
He said Pakistan Telecommunication Company Ltd (PTCL) shares would rise on higher expected earnings after the government allowed it to adjust its telephone call tariffs.

Ahmed said the budget had reaffirmed previously announced government policies, but said the market had already discounted it. "The index will come under pressure because the market is overbought and players have already accounted for the budget."
Usma Shoaib of KASB & Co said the budget was friendly towards business and ordinary people.
"Shares of tractor companies will rise because of a reduction of import duty on completely knocked down kits for local assemblers to 10 percent from 20 percent," he said.
Dealer Zaina Nowsherwan said it was a good budget in the circumstances because no new taxes had been imposed, while various sectors had received concessions.

But Sara Taseer, a dealer at First Capital, said it was too good to be true. "It is a very volatile situation for the market. A lot of relief has been given to various sectors and there are concerns as to how the government will generate revenue and what will be the IMF's reaction," she said.
"Agriculture tax has not been imposed, the defence budget had not been capped. There are no new taxes. In fact they have slashed duties and taxes on a number of sectors."
She said there were fears that acute financial problems might prevent the government from pursuing its chosen course.
